item.title: When to expect your March Social Security benefits
item.description: Social Security recipients can expect a mostly regular payment schedule in March.

item.title: Chicago overcharged $163 million in parking ticket fees, judge rules
item.description: A Cook County judge ruled that the City of Chicago overcharged residents for parking tickets by $163 million over 10 years, and refunds must be issued.

item.title: Robert Cosby Jr., son of 'Real Housewives of Salt Lake City' star Mary Cosby, passes away at 23
item.description: "Though our hearts ache, we take comfort in God's promise and in knowing he is finally at peace," the reality star wrote of her son's passing.

item.title: Waymo's self-driving cars map Chicago streets, but no driverless rides yet
item.description: Waymo announced its fleet is mapping Chicago streets, a critical first step toward bringing the self-driving cars to the city.

item.title: Nursing assistant arrested following alleged sexual assault of health care facility resident with physical, mental disabilities
item.description: A nursing assistant has been denied pre-trial release after he allegedly sexually assaulted a resident with physical and mental disabilities at a Bloomingdale heath care facility.

item.title: How the bump in burglaries impacts Chicago businesses
item.description: Chicago has seen nearly 10,000 business burglaries since 2021, with an average of over 30 per week, causing pain for business owners and prompting the Cook County Sheriff's office to launch an Organized Retail Crime Team to bust the bosses of the crime rings.

item.title: Lawsuit filed against Oswego District 308 for teacher's alleged grooming, sexual misconduct
item.description: Four former Oswego High School students have filed a lawsuit alleging years of grooming, sexual harassment, and sexual misconduct by a former teacher and coach, which the district allegedly knew about and failed to stop.
